items.stem: In the PICO framework used to frame an answerable question, what does the 'C' most commonly represent?

options.rationale: Correct: C is the comparison or comparator, the alternative against which the intervention is weighed.
PICO does not include 'cause'; the comparator is what C denotes.
The condition is captured in the Population (P), not in C.
A conclusion is an output of appraisal, not an element of the PICO question.

items.stem: Evidence-based practice integrates best available evidence with which TWO other elements? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: professional expertise is one of the three pillars of EBP.
Correct: patient values and preferences are an essential pillar alongside evidence and expertise.

options.text: The most senior colleague's personal opinion
options.rationale: Deferring to seniority alone is authority-based, not evidence-based, practice.

options.text: Whatever option is cheapest to implement
options.rationale: Cost may inform feasibility but is not a defining pillar of EBP.

items.stem: Considering only study design, which source generally sits highest in the hierarchy of evidence for a question about treatment effectiveness?

options.text: A systematic review of randomised controlled trials
options.rationale: Correct: a well-conducted systematic review of RCTs generally sits at the top for treatment-effectiveness questions.
Expert opinion sits near the bottom of the hierarchy because it is most prone to bias.
A case report describes one instance and cannot establish effectiveness.

options.text: A narrative commentary with no stated methods
options.rationale: Without a stated method the work cannot be appraised and ranks low.

items.explanation: Correct: a well-conducted systematic review of RCTs generally sits at the top for treatment-effectiveness questions.
